column3: The Hebrew has singular “the blessing” and “the curse” and says to bring these back to the heart; BSB has plural “blessings and curses” and says “call them to mind.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names “the LORD your God” twice and repeats the returning root before the gathering; BSB begins with “He” and states the gathering without a separate “again.”
The Hebrew says “the edge of the heavens,” names “the LORD your God,” and repeats “from there”; BSB has “the farthest horizon,” “He,” and one “from there.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular “heart” for both you and your “seed” and repeats “the LORD your God”; BSB has plural “hearts,” “descendants,” and “Him” in the second clause.
The Hebrew separately names “your enemies” and “those who hate you”; BSB combines these as “your enemies who hate you.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew has singular “your hand” and repeats “fruit” for womb, livestock, and ground; BSB uses plural “hands” and varies “fruit,” “offspring,” and “produce.” The Hebrew says the LORD rejoices over you “for good”; BSB says He delights “in your goodness.”
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD’s “voice” and repeats “the LORD your God”; BSB says “obey the LORD your God” and then uses “Him.”
The Hebrew says the commandment is not “far away”; BSB says it is not “beyond your reach.”
The Hebrew says to “cause us to hear it”; BSB says to “proclaim it.”
The Hebrew says to “cause us to hear it”; BSB says to “proclaim it.”
The Hebrew ends with “to do it”; BSB says “so that you may obey it.”

The Hebrew uses the image of “your seed”; BSB says “your descendants.”

The Hebrew calls Him both “your life” and “the length of your days”; BSB turns the latter into the action “He will prolong your life.” The Hebrew also explicitly names “His voice,” while BSB says “obey Him.”
